newsitem.title: NIGER: Niger election talks break down, deadline passes.
newsitem.headline: Niger election talks break down, deadline passes.

text.p: Talks between Niger's government and opposition on next month's legislative election collapsed on Monday, with each side blaming the other and the government insisting that the November 23 poll date would stand.
The Monday 1800 GMT deadline for registration of candidates, extended several times, passed without the opposition putting forward any names, sources close to the interior ministry said.
"Despite numerous attempts since September 26, it has not been possible to reach agreement," Interior Minister Idi Ango Omar said in a government statement.

The opposition later accused the government of breaking off the talks unilaterally when the two sides had reached agreement on most of the points dividing them. "In reality, the government never intended to negotiate," ousted prime minister Hama Amadou said afterwards.

Opposition parties, angry over the conduct of the July presidential election won by coup maker Ibrahim Bare Mainassara, let Wednesday's previous deadline pass without registering and without naming representatives to a new electoral commission.

The November 23 election of the 83 members of the new national assembly is part of Mainassara's efforts to return the mainly Moslem West African state to multi-party politics following his coup in January.
"The president and government urge all citizens in a spirit of patriotism to put the general interest first and ensure that democracy triumphs," the government statement said.
Mainassara, who toppled an elected president and government, scrapped the independent national electoral commission part way through the July presidential election.

Eight opposition parties, grouped in the Front for the Restoration and Defence of Democracy, want restoration of the scrapped electoral commission and a reconstituted constitutional chamber of the supreme court, which ratifies poll results.
